entries.title: Psalms 80:1
segments:
A prayer of God's people in deep distress occasioned by the oppression of foreign enemies, in which the transfer of Israel from Egypt to Canaan is beautifully set forth under the allegory of a vine.  It belongs apparently to the later period before the Babylonish captivity. In the opinion of many, its occasion was the overthrow of the kingdom of Israel by the Assyrians. 
 
  Joseph; the Israelites.

entries.title: Psalms 80:2
segments: Before Ephraim and Benjamin and Manasseh; during the sojourn of the Israelites in the wilderness of Arabia, these three tribes encamped together on the west side of the tabernacle,
; and in the order of march, they followed the Kohathites who bore the ark of the covenant, the symbol of God's presence,
; thus having "the ark of the covenant of the Lord of hosts, which dwelleth between the cherubim," immediately before them.

entries.title: Psalms 80:3
segments: The light of God's countenance is the greatest blessing that any can enjoy, and is most earnestly desired and sought by his obedient people.

entries.title: Psalms 80:5
segments: Bread of tears; deep afflictions, causing many to weep.

entries.title: Psalms 80:8
segments:
A vine; the church, as embodied in the nation of Israel. 
 
For all her prosperity the church is dependent on the grace of God, while her sins are the cause of all her sorrows.

entries.title: Psalms 80:10
segments: And the boughs thereof were like the goodly cedars; or, and with the boughs thereof, the cedars of God [were covered.]

entries.title: Psalms 80:11
segments:
The sea; the Mediterranean. 
 
  The river; Euphrates.

entries.title: Psalms 80:13
segments: The boar--and the wild beast; representing the heathen by whom the Israelites were overcome.

entries.title: Psalms 80:15
segments: Help for the guilty is laid upon One who is mighty to save, who came to take away sin by the sacrifice of himself, and who ever lives to make intercession for all who come unto God through him.

entries.title: Psalms 80:17
segments: The son of man; the Messiah, for whose advent God's people looked to deliver them from their troubles.
